root_cause: cape_cin overwrites the environmental temperature and parcel_profile variables with virtual-temperature equivalents before calling lfc and el. Those functions then compute the LCL constraint from their temperature inputs, so the LCL calculation receives parcel/environment virtual temperature as if it were ordinary air temperature, biasing the LCL pressure lower and potentially forcing LFC/EL selection too high.
approach: Keep using virtual-temperature profiles for the LFC/EL intersection tests used by CAPE/CIN, but do not let lfc and el recompute the LCL from those virtual temperatures. Add a small optional LCL pressure override to lfc and el, and pass the already-computed real-temperature pressure_lcl from cape_cin into both calls. This preserves the virtual-temperature correction for buoyancy while applying the LCL floor from the original thermodynamic profile.
tests_to_add: No new test within the 7-line patch budget; if the budget is relaxed, add a regression test where cape_cin with a moist surface parcel uses the same real-temperature LCL pressure constraint while retaining virtual-temperature CAPE/CIN integration.
risk_notes: Adding optional public parameters to lfc and el should be backward compatible, but the exact parameter names should avoid implying users normally need to supply them.
out_of_scope_observations: No broader refactoring of CAPE/CIN integration or lfc/el selection modes is planned.
